finding_key: packages/documentation/sheets/datasources.md::new datasources doc states a security model the code does not enforce: collaborators do execute queries with the creator's stored credentials
evidence: The new doc's "Good to know" bullet (packages/documentation/sheets/datasources.md, last section, ~line 45) claims "The connection belongs to the person who created it. Collaborators can see the query and its last results, but run their own connection to execute it." The backend does not implement that isolation: `POST datasources/:id/query` only does `findRaw(id)` + `workspaceService.assertMember(ds.workspaceId, req.user.id)` (datasource.controller.ts, executeQuery) and then `DataSourceService.executeQuery` builds the client via `createClient(ds)` with `decrypt(ds.password)` — i.e. every workspace member runs queries against the creator's stored credentials, with no per-user credential prompt anywhere in the datasource API (frontend/src/api/datasources.ts just POSTs the query). So the documented ownership/isolation statement contradicts the code as written; it is a documentation inaccuracy about a security-relevant model rather than a code defect (workspace-membership scoping may well be intended).
